question.text: Per the AIF Cat I/II Distributors (XIX-A) workbook, in a PE transaction the term sheet is non-binding. Which of the following best describes the role of the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA) and the Shareholders' Agreement (SHA)?

answer.text: Both are non-binding preliminary documents like the term sheet

Both are definitive (legally binding) agreements: the Share Subscription Agreement governs the actual investment terms (price, payment, conditions precedent, representations and warranties, indemnities), and the Shareholders' Agreement governs the ongoing rights and obligations of the shareholders post-investment
Both are internal fund-management documents not seen by the investee company
Both are regulatory filings made with the stock exchange before closing

explanation.text: The Logic: The XIX-A workbook distinguishes a non-binding term sheet from the definitive agreements such as the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA) and the Shareholders' Agreement (SHA). The SSA contains the binding investment terms; the SHA governs post-closing governance rights between shareholders. The Trap: The "Share Purchase Agreement / SPA" label common in M&A texts is not the specific term used in the XIX-A workbook; the workbook uses "Share Subscription Agreement" alongside the Shareholders' Agreement. Term sheets are non-binding; SSAs/SHAs are not internal-only or exchange filings. Note: The XIX-A workbook also identifies "subscription agreement" as a definitive agreement in its sample-question framing.
